adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158 — EventManager is built from the *caller's* credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)) instead of the booking organizer's (fetched at line 34 and never used), so when an attendee or team owner adds guests the calendar update targets the wrong account and silently no-ops.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler allows non-organizers (attendees or team admins/owners) to add guests. However, the calendar update is performed via `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })`, where `user` is the *caller* (`ctx.user`). The booking organizer is fetched (`organizer = await prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow(...)`) and the booking query also includes `user: { ... credentials: true }`, but neither is used to build the `EventManager`. If the caller is not the organizer, this means `updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` will run under the caller’s calendar credentials rather than the organizer’s, so the calendar event update can target the wrong account and may fail/no-op due to missing permissions or missing event reference in the caller’s calendars.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92 — Attendee rows are committed before updateCalendarAttendees/emails with no transaction or compensation, so a calendar failure leaves guests persisted but uninvited and unnotified, and retrying is rejected with BAD_REQUEST "emails_must_be_unique_valid" — an unrecoverable half-applied state.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In addGuests.handler.ts the code persists new attendees via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` before calling `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` and before sending emails. There is no surrounding transaction and no compensation/rollback if `updateCalendarAttendees` throws (it is not inside a try/catch). In that failure case, the DB now contains the added attendees but calendar updates/emails were not performed. On a retry with the same guest list, `uniqueGuests` filters out emails already in `booking.attendees`, and if all requested guests were already inserted, `uniqueGuests.length === 0` triggers `TRPCError({ code: "BAD_REQUEST", message: "emails_must_be_unique_valid" })`, preventing a straightforward retry to complete the missing side effects. This matches the finding's “half-applied state” description.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — guests array has no max length and no rate limiting, and authz accepts any booking attendee (self-obtained by booking any public event type), turning the endpoint into an authenticated mail-bomb/spam relay sending ICS invites from the product's domain to arbitrary addresses.

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` mutation accepts `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max(...)` bound (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts), and the handler will create attendees and trigger calendar updates + outbound emails based on that list (addGuests.handler.ts calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` and `sendAddGuestsEmails`). Authorization explicitly allows any authenticated booking attendee (`isAttendee`) to call the endpoint, not just the organizer/admin. Given a public event type, an attacker can become an attendee by booking once, then submit a very large list of arbitrary emails to generate many emails/ICS invites from the system. The “no rate limiting” part isn’t directly verifiable from the diff, but the lack of per-request bounds plus permissive authz and email sending is a real abuse/spam risk introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:169 — Email failures are swallowed by `catch { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails") }` (error object discarded), so the mutation returns success and the UI toasts "Guests added" when zero notifications were delivered and nothing alerts anyone.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, after successfully updating attendees and updating the calendar, the code wraps `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` in a `try { ... } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }`. This catch discards the error object and does not rethrow or return an error, so the mutation still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }` even if all email sending fails. On the client, the mutation `onSuccess` shows `showToast(t("guests_added"), "success")`, so the UI will indicate success regardless of notification delivery. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — The server schema never dedupes within `guests` and the existing-attendee filter is a read-then-write with no unique constraint or transaction, so one request containing the same email twice — or two concurrent requests — creates duplicate attendee rows and duplicate emails.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — sendAddGuestsEmails is passed the raw `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests`, so resubmitting an email that is already an attendee routes that person to AttendeeScheduledEmail (a fresh "booking confirmed" mail with a REQUEST ICS) instead of the add-guests notice.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the handler computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering out emails already in `booking.attendees` (and blacklisted emails) and uses `uniqueGuests` to create new attendee records. However, it later calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the original raw `guests` input. In email-manager.ts, `sendAddGuestsEmails` uses the passed `newGuests` list to decide per attendee: if `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` it sends `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (the “scheduled/confirmed” style email with REQUEST ICS), otherwise it sends `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` (the add-guests notice). Therefore, if the input `guests` contains an email that was already an attendee (which is allowed unless all entries are already attendees, in which case it throws), that existing attendee will incorrectly match `includes(...)` and receive `AttendeeScheduledEmail` again instead of the add-guests notice. In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` call is wrapped in `try { ... } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }`. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — sendAddGuestsEmails` is passed the raw `guests` input rather than the computed `uniqueGuests`, so the handler and email-manager use two different notions of "new guest".

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler computes `uniqueGuests` by removing already-attending emails and blacklisted ones, and only `uniqueGuests` are persisted via `createMany` and included in `evt.attendees`. However it calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the raw input array `guests`, not `uniqueGuests`. In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, the `newGuests` list is used to decide per-attendee which email to send (`newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`). If the user submits an email that was already an attendee, that attendee will still be in `evt.attendees` and will be incorrectly treated as a “new guest” for email purposes. This is a concrete mismatch between persisted “new guests” and emailed “new guests” introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — guests` array has no max length (and no server-side dedupe), so one request can create unbounded attendee rows and fan out one email + ICS per attendee via an unbounded `Promise.all`.

adjudication.rationale: The server-side input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` only enforces `guests` as `z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max(...)` bound. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the incoming `guests` array (so the same new email repeated will remain repeated). The handler then does `attendees.createMany` with that data and calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, which in `email-manager.ts` builds an `emailsToSend` array that grows with `calendarEvent.attendees` and executes `await Promise.all(emailsToSend)`. This means a single request can attempt to create a large number of attendee rows and fan out a large number of concurrent email/ICS sends, with no hard server-side cap and no server-side uniqueness enforcement for the request payload.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:114 — getTranslation` is called once per attendee instead of once per distinct locale, reloading the same i18n bundle N times for every add-guests call.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the code builds attendeesListPromises by mapping over every attendee and calling `getTranslation(attendee.locale ?? "en", "common")` inside that map. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:38 — Booking query eagerly includes `user.credentials` (large encrypted key blobs, one row per connected app) but only `user.destinationCalendar` is used; credentials are refetched later by `getUsersCredentials`.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the `prisma.booking.findFirst` call includes `user: { include: { destinationCalendar: true, credentials: true } }`, but within this handler the only field subsequently read from `booking.user` is `booking.user?.destinationCalendar` when building `evt.destinationCalendar`. The handler later fetches credentials separately via `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`, and never references `booking.user.credentials`. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:47 — isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner` are awaited sequentially and run on every call, including non-team bookings where `teamId ?? 0` guarantees no match.

adjudication.rationale:
In addGuests.handler.ts the code is:

```ts
const isTeamAdminOrOwner =
  (await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) &&
  (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0));
```

This does await `isTeamAdmin` first, but `isTeamOwner` is only executed if `isTeamAdmin` returns truthy because of `&&` short-circuiting. So the finding’s claim that both checks “run on every call” (including non-team bookings) is not verifiably true from the diff. Also, the sequential awaiting is not inherently a defect here; it avoids the second call unless needed. While passing `teamId ?? 0` may result in an unnecessary `isTeamAdmin(..., 0)` call for non-team bookings, that’s a minor potential inefficiency and the proposed finding overstates it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` is awaited un-guarded after the attendee rows are already committed, so a calendar/video provider failure throws and leaves the DB and the external calendar permanently divergent with no rollback or compensating write

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the code first commits new attendees to the database via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` and only afterwards calls `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` without any try/catch, transaction, rollback, or compensating write. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws (e.g., calendar provider/API failure), the TRPC mutation will error out but the DB has already been updated, leaving internal booking attendees out of sync with the external calendar state until some separate resync occurs. The diff shows no mechanism to revert the DB change or retry/mark pending sync, so the finding is a real correctness/consistency issue in the introduced code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:81 — A retry after a post-commit failure at line 165 is rejected with BAD_REQUEST `emails_must_be_unique_valid` because the guests are now attendees, so the operation is unrecoverable from the UI

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the DB update that creates new attendees happens before `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and before the email send. That `updateCalendarAttendees` call is not wrapped in a try/catch or transaction; if it throws after the `prisma.booking.update` has succeeded, the mutation errors out while the guests are already persisted. On retry, `uniqueGuests` filters out emails that are already in `booking.attendees`, so `uniqueGuests.length === 0` triggers a `TRPCError` BAD_REQUEST with message `emails_must_be_unique_valid`, making the operation non-idempotent and effectively unrecoverable from the UI for the same input.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:169 — Email failures are swallowed with `console.log` that drops the error object and bypasses `@calcom/lib/logger`, and the mutation still returns success so nobody learns the guests were never notified

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the email send is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }`. The catch block discards the `err` object (no stack/details) and uses `console.log` instead of any structured/logger facility. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:95 — The attendee `createMany` and the external calendar/email side effects are not wrapped in a transaction or any outbox/background job, so any failure after line 106 leaves a partially applied change

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the code persists new attendees via prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}}) and then performs side effects: EventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking) and sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests). These operations are not wrapped in a database transaction with compensating logic, nor is there an outbox/background job pattern. If updateCalendarAttendees throws (it is not in a try/catch) after the DB write succeeds, the booking will have the new attendees stored but the external calendar update won’t happen, leaving state partially applied. Even email sending is best-effort (caught and logged), so DB changes can be committed without notifications.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/emails/email-manager.ts:549 — Promise.all` rejects on the first failing recipient and the single rejection is all the caller ever sees, so per-recipient delivery failures are not individually reported (Promise.allSettled would surface them)

adjudication.rationale: In `sendAddGuestsEmails` the code does `await Promise.all(emailsToSend)`, but there is no per-recipient reporting mechanism in the function’s API anyway (it returns `void` and doesn’t expose results). Also, the caller (`addGuests.handler.ts`) wraps `sendAddGuestsEmails` in a `try/catch` and intentionally swallows any thrown error, so switching to `Promise.allSettled` would be a behavioral/design choice rather than a clear, verifiable defect introduced by this diff. Additionally, `Promise.all` does not prevent other already-created send promises from running; it only determines how the aggregate await resolves/rejects.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:52 — Any attendee (matched by raw `attendee.email === user.email`, with no verified-ownership binding) is authorized to mutate an arbitrary booking they only supply the id for, adding attacker-chosen recipients to someone else's booking.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:77 — BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS check lowercases the blacklist but compares against the raw guest string, so `Blocked@X.com` bypasses the blocklist (same for the duplicate-attendee check on line 76).

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, blacklistedGuestEmails are normalized to lowercase (`map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`), but in the `uniqueGuests` filter the code compares `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` and `guest === attendee.email` using the raw `guest` string. Since neither `guest` nor `attendee.email` is lowercased/normalized before comparison, case-variant inputs (e.g., `Blocked@X.com`) can bypass the blacklist and can also evade the existing-attendee check if stored emails differ only by case. This is a concrete correctness/security gap visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — guests` array has no max length, no normalization and the mutation has no rate limiting, so one call can persist and email hundreds of attacker-controlled addresses (ICS-attached mail from the app's domain) — spam/mail-bomb relay.

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` mutation accepts `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no upper bound and no normalization (e.g., lowercasing/trim). In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler persists all provided guest emails via `createMany` and then triggers `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, which results in sending emails to attendees based on the (potentially large) input list. Because an authenticated attendee is allowed to call this mutation (`isAttendee` path), a user can submit a very large array of attacker-controlled addresses and cause the app to send a large volume of ICS-attached emails from the app’s domain (mail-bomb/spam relay risk). The rate-limiting claim is not directly shown in the diff (could exist globally), but the unbounded input + immediate email fanout is a verifiable issue introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:46 — Team authorization is composed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)` over `booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0`, an incorrect check that both denies legitimate team admins and silently probes teamId 0 for non-team bookings instead of short-circuiting.

adjudication.rationale:
In addGuests.handler.ts the permission flag is computed as:

```ts
const isTeamAdminOrOwner =
  (await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) &&
  (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0));
```

This is internally inconsistent with the variable name and typical intent (“admin OR owner”). Using `&&` means only users who are *both* team admin and team owner pass, which will incorrectly deny legitimate team admins who aren’t owners. Also, when `booking.eventType?.teamId` is undefined/null (non-team booking), it still calls both queries with `0` instead of short-circuiting, which is a concrete, verifiable defect (unnecessary/possibly incorrect auth checks against an invalid teamId).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158 — EventManager is constructed from the *caller's* identity and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` to update the *organizer's* calendar/video event references, so a non-organizer caller's OAuth credentials are used against another user's external event ids.

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuestsHandler` explicitly allows non-organizers to call it (`isAttendee` check permits any existing attendee). Yet when updating the external calendar it does `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and constructs `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })` where `user` is the *caller* (`ctx.user`). It then calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` using the booking (which belongs to `booking.userId` / organizer and includes `references`, `destinationCalendar`, etc.). This means an attendee (or other permitted non-organizer) will attempt the calendar update using their own OAuth credentials against the booking’s external event references, which are typically tied to the organizer’s calendar integration. That is a concrete correctness/security issue introduced by the diff: the identity/credentials used for the calendar mutation are not aligned with the resource owner (organizer/booking).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/emails/email-manager.ts:542 — Newly added guests are sent the full AttendeeScheduledEmail including video call url/password and the complete attendee list of a booking they had no prior relationship to, and the caller may be a mere attendee.
matched_golden_ids: The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The golden issue is that sendAddGuestsEmails mis-determines which attendees should receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail because it iterates over the full calendarEvent.attendees while using newGuests (input guests list) for the inclusion check, leading to incorrect recipients. The candidate issue describes the consequence of that same logic error: newly added guests receiving the full AttendeeScheduledEmail (with video URL/password and full attendee list) when they should get the add-guests email. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:44 — Booking is fetched unscoped and NOT_FOUND is thrown before the permission check, giving an authenticated user a booking-id existence oracle (NOT_FOUND vs FORBIDDEN).

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the handler first queries prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId } ... }) without scoping it to the requesting user/team (line ~44 in the new file). It then immediately throws TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" }) if no booking exists, and only afterwards checks whether the user is team admin/owner, organizer, or attendee and throws FORBIDDEN if not. Because this is an authedProcedure, any authenticated user can probe booking IDs and distinguish "booking exists but I lack access" (FORBIDDEN) from "booking does not exist" (NOT_FOUND), which is a booking existence oracle.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:46 — No test covers the four permission branches (team-admin, organizer, attendee, stranger), so the `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)` AND (should be OR) silently kills the team-admin path.

adjudication.rationale:
In addGuests.handler.ts the permission flag is computed as:
```ts
const isTeamAdminOrOwner =
  (await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) &&
  (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0));
```
This requires the user to be BOTH team admin AND team owner. Given the variable name `isTeamAdminOrOwner` and the finding’s claim that this “kills the team-admin path”, this is a verifiable logic issue in the diff: a team admin who is not also an owner will fail this check and be denied unless they happen to be organizer/attendee. The “no test covers the four permission branches” portion is not verifiable from the diff, but the AND-vs-OR permission bug is present in the changed code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — Uniqueness/validity is enforced only by the client-side zod refine in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26 with no test asserting the server rejects a duplicate-email payload sent directly to the mutation.

adjudication.rationale: The server-side input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` only validates `guests` as `z.array(z.string().email())` and does not enforce uniqueness. In the server handler, `uniqueGuests` filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails, but it does not deduplicate duplicates within the incoming `guests` array (it never checks against already-selected items). Therefore a direct mutation payload like `guests: ["a@b.com","a@b.com"]` can pass validation and be written via `createMany`, meaning uniqueness is effectively only enforced by the client-side `refine` in `AddGuestsDialog` and is not guaranteed on the server.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — The dedupe/blacklist filter and its all-filtered BAD_REQUEST branch are untested, hiding the case-sensitivity holes (`guest === attendee.email` and `includes(guest)` against a lowercased list).

adjudication.rationale: The handler lowercases `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` entries (`map(...toLowerCase())`) but compares them against the raw `guest` string (`!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`), and it also compares guests to existing attendee emails with a case-sensitive equality (`guest === attendee.email`). This creates a real correctness/security gap: a blacklisted email (or an existing attendee email) can bypass filtering by using different casing (e.g., `Bad@Example.com`). adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/emails/email-manager.ts:541 — No test exercises the new-guest vs existing-attendee template routing, so the handler passing raw `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests` (addGuests.handler.ts:168) mails existing attendees an AttendeeScheduledEmail.

adjudication.rationale: Real issue: `addGuests.handler.ts` computes `uniqueGuests` (filters out already-attending + blacklisted) and only adds those to the booking, but then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the *raw* input list. In `sendAddGuestsEmails` (`email-manager.ts`), the routing logic uses `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` to decide whether an attendee gets `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (treated as newly added) vs `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` (existing attendee notification). If the caller submits a mix of existing attendee emails plus at least one new email, the existing attendee email will still be present in `guests`, so that existing attendee will incorrectly receive `AttendeeScheduledEmail`. Passing `uniqueGuests` would avoid that. The “no test exercises…” part is not directly verifiable from the diff, but the behavioral bug is.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts:28 — Subject line reads `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` with no test for the zero-attendee or blank-name guest case (new guests are created with `name: ""`).

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts`, the subject interpolates `name: this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` with no guard. In the new add-guests flow (`addGuests.handler.ts`), newly-created guests are explicitly created with `name: ""`, and the `CalendarEvent.attendees` array is built directly from the booking attendees returned by Prisma without any guaranteed ordering. That means `attendees[0]` can reasonably be a newly-added guest with a blank name, producing an empty/incorrect subject. Additionally, if `calEvent.attendees` were ever empty, this would throw at runtime.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:33 — No component test for the invalid-email flow; `isInvalidEmail` is never reset to false on a subsequent successful submit, so the error banner persists on reopen.

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog`, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when `ZAddGuestsInputSchema.safeParse(multiEmailValue)` fails, but it is never set back to `false` on the successful path (`addGuestsMutation.onSuccess`). `onSuccess` closes the dialog and resets `multiEmailValue`, but does not clear `isInvalidEmail`, so if a user previously triggered the invalid-email banner, it will remain `true` and the error banner will appear again when the dialog is reopened (component stays mounted).
